checks.summary: Raised RuntimeError private Neo4j graph changed during cleanup; did not silently pass.

review_conclusions: No store.clear call remains in the new harness. Its private cleanup checks a Pa113N plus 10 lowercase hex label, uses an explicit matching Neo4j database, and deletes only that label with LIMIT 100 inside separate execute_write transactions.

The helper counts initial nodes, rejects graphs needing more than its finite max_batches before deletion, requires positive progress and a terminal zero batch, and checks removed total against the initial count.
Neo4j close still attempts private constraint and index removal and driver.close when batched deletion fails; loader and measurement exceptions retain primary identity with cleanup failure chained.
The report distinguishes requested entity nodes from actual loaded nodes per backend; smoke6 records 200 requested and 400 loaded across all three backends.
Depth-1/2 walk and filtered-leg parity precede timing; controller verifies same candidate source across old and refreshed interpreters with distinct lock hashes and owned Neo4j container stability.
resolved_findings: v2 normal cleanup called Neo4jGraphStore.clear in one large transaction and failed with Java heap OOM after full old-lock measurements; v3 replaces only benchmark-private cleanup with bounded exact-label batches.
remaining_limitations: V3 has only completed 1k compiled plus 200 mention edge paired smoke; the full 100k plus 20k paired timing has not been rerun and no performance result is approved.
Neo4jGraphStore.clear in the runtime remains unchanged and its large-graph single-transaction limitation remains; this review approves only the benchmark-private cleanup.
The prior full old-lock run produced no final report because its normal Neo4j cleanup failed; those partial timings must not be relabeled as a successful comparison.
verdict: PASS: R1 approves frozen v3 two-file harness for distinct R2 review; full paired timing remains held.
